Age-related macular degeneration (AMD)

A 78-person sham-controlled trial reported a 3.75-letter between-group visual-acuity difference and reduced drusen measures at 12 months. LIGHTSITE III follow-up reports showed visual-acuity gains, but the 13- and 24-month publications describe the same cohort and do not independently confirm long-term progression effects.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

A 78-person sham-controlled trial reported a 3.75-letter between-group visual-acuity difference and reduced drusen measures at 12 months. LIGHTSITE III follow-up reports showed visual-acuity gains, but the 13- and 24-month publications describe the same cohort and do not independently confirm long-term progression effects.

Summary of the Evidence

The category contains 51 database rows and 50 unique titles after one duplicate is merged. Records include randomized trials, non-randomized studies, case reports, animal and laboratory work, reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, and a guideline. Method tags overlap. LIGHTSITE III articles at 13 and 24 months report follow-up from the same participant cohort; a related economic analysis is not a new clinical cohort.

Human and clinical evidence

Iovino and colleagues reported a multicenter, double-masked sham-controlled trial with 78 participants and 138 eyes followed for 12 months. PBM reduced drusen measures while sham eyes increased, and the between-group visual-acuity difference was 3.75 letters. The LIGHTSITE III 24-month report described modest visual-acuity gains and fewer geographic-atrophy cases; its 13- and 24-month papers are repeated follow-up reports, not independent trials. These findings should not be combined as separate cohorts (Iovino et al. 2026 Jaffe et al. 2026).

Animal evidence

Eleven titles are tagged as animal research, including mouse and rat models. They provide preclinical retinal evidence but do not establish visual benefit or prevention of progression in people.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

One title is tagged as in-vitro research. It is laboratory evidence and should not be treated as a separate patient trial.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The LIGHTSITE III protocol used 590, 660, and 850 nm light, with treatment three times weekly for three to five weeks every four months over 24 months. Other clinical records do not report a consistent protocol. Study designs, retinal stage, follow-up, and outcome definitions vary, so these device-specific schedules limit direct comparison.

Interpretation

Controlled studies report visual-acuity or retinal-structure findings in dry AMD, but the number of independent cohorts is smaller than the publication count suggests. Longer follow-up and independent confirmation are needed before concluding that PBM prevents progression to geographic atrophy.

Evidence strength in source summaryVisual acuity and retinal biomarkers in dry AMD: Low to moderate Prevention of geographic atrophy or long-term progression: Low
Publications and records50 unique titles from 51 database rows, one duplicate merged

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The category includes randomized and observational clinical studies, but repeated reports share cohorts, including the LIGHTSITE III 13- and 24-month publications. A recent sham-controlled trial reported better visual acuity and drusen measures, while follow-up and progression outcomes remain uncertain. Independent trials with longer follow-up are needed to confirm disease-modifying effects.
